description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Join the founding engineering team building an AI agent framework for farm operations. You will work closely with AI leadership to design and deliver production agents that support real business decisions across multiple farms.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and own the agent framework, including roles, tools, permissions, approvals, and a runtime for tasks that span multiple days.

 - Build memory and context systems that give agents relevant farm-specific knowledge, including information not formally documented.

 - Develop code automation that enables agents to write and reuse code for recurring tasks, with human oversight for unexpected cases.

 - Create evaluations and safety measures that make agents reliable for business use and track their improvement over time.

 - Build agent tools on the data layer and integrate machine learning insights into the framework.

 - Work with farm teams to observe the system in use and improve it based on feedback.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Two to four years of engineering experience, including shipping production LLM agents or agentic workflows that people rely on.

 - Experience building agents with tool use, orchestration, context and memory design, and evaluation.

 - Strong Python skills and comfort with PostgreSQL, asynchronous systems, and workflow engines.

 - Experience writing evaluations and critically reviewing AI-generated code, with the ability to handle system design independently.

 - Experience with durable workflow engines such as Temporal, agent observability and tracing, or security topics such as prompt injection and permissions is beneficial.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary is $170,000 to $200,000 annually, plus 1% equity with four-year vesting and a one-year cliff. Healthcare and access to AI coding tools, models, and hardware are provided. Visa sponsorship is not available; candidates must already be authorized to work in the United States.


LOCATION

On-site in San Francisco, California, five days per week, with approximately one week of quarterly travel to farms in Washington, Oregon, and California.
